questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Our much-awaited annual function will be held _________ the coming Friday.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Our much-awaited annual function will be held _________ the coming Friday.
questions.solution:
The context of the sentence is about specifying the day on which an event will take place. The blank requires a preposition of time that is used for specific days of the week.

The correct option is "on." The preposition "on" is always used before specific days (e.g., on Monday, on Friday) and dates (e.g., on 25th December).

The other options are incorrect: "in" is used for longer periods like months, years, and seasons (e.g., in July, in 2024). "at" is used for specific times of the day (e.g., at 5 PM). "since" is used to denote a starting point in time.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "Our much-awaited annual function will be held on the coming Friday."

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. She has been suffering / from a severe headache / for last Monday / and needs to see a doctor.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

She has been suffering / from a severe headache / for last Monday / and needs to see a doctor.

options.text: and needs to see a doctor
options.html: and needs to see a doctor

questions.solution:
The error is in the use of the preposition "for" with a specific point in time. The preposition "for" is used to indicate a duration or period of time (e.g., for two days). The preposition "since" is used to indicate a starting point in time (e.g., since Monday, since 2020). "Last Monday" is a specific starting point, so "since" should be used.

Correct sentence: She has been suffering from a severe headache since last Monday and needs to see a doctor.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option c).

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Despite of working very hard, / he could not pass / the difficult entrance examination / this year.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Despite of working very hard, / he could not pass / the difficult entrance examination / this year.
questions.solution:
The error lies in the use of the preposition "of" after "Despite." The word "Despite" is a preposition that means "without being affected by" and is not followed by "of." The phrase "in spite of" has the same meaning and is correctly followed by "of." One can use either "Despite" (without "of") or "In spite of."

Correct sentence: Despite working very hard, he could not pass the difficult entrance examination this year.

OR

In spite of working very hard, he could not pass the difficult entrance examination this year.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option a).

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The manager did not approve with the new marketing strategy proposed by the junior executive team.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The manager did not approve with the new marketing strategy proposed by the junior executive team.
questions.solution:
The error lies in the preposition "with" used after the verb "approve". The correct preposition to follow "approve" when it means 'to agree to' or 'to accept as satisfactory' is "of". The phrasal verb is "approve of".

Correct sentence: The manager did not approve of the new marketing strategy proposed by the junior executive team.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Note:

Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The students were asked to abstain from talk during the examination.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The students were asked to abstain from talk during the examination.
questions.solution:
The error in the underlined segment is the form of the verb "talk." The verb "abstain" is followed by the preposition "from," which in turn must be followed by a gerund (the -ing form of a verb) when an action is mentioned.

The original segment uses the base form "talk" instead of the gerund "talking."

Option d) from talking during the is correct. It correctly uses the structure "abstain from" followed by the gerund "talking."

Option a) with talking during the uses the wrong preposition "with."

Option b) to talk during the uses the infinitive "to talk," which is incorrect after "abstain from."

Option c) for talking in the uses the wrong preposition "for."

Correct Sentence: The students were asked to abstain from talking during the examination.

Hence, the most appropriate choice is d) from talking during the.

Note: Gerund: Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. Here, 'talking' functions as the object of the preposition 'from'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. _________ being a talented musician, he is also an excellent painter.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

_________ being a talented musician, he is also an excellent painter.
questions.solution:
The context of the sentence is to add another piece of information about a person's talents. The blank requires a preposition that means "in addition to" or "as well as."

The correct option is "Besides." The preposition "Besides" (with an 's') means "in addition to" or "apart from."

The other options are incorrect: "Beside" (without an 's') is a preposition of place meaning "next to." "Behind" and "Below" are also prepositions of place and are not logical in this context.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "Besides being a talented musician, he is also an excellent painter."

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My uncle is a famous businessman who deals _________ antique home furniture.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My uncle is a famous businessman who deals _________ antique home furniture.
questions.solution:
The sentence describes a businessman's area of trade. The blank requires a preposition to complete the phrasal verb "deal," specifying the nature of the business.

The correct option is "in." The phrasal verb "deal in something" means to buy and sell a particular product as a business.

The other options are incorrect: "deal with" means to handle a problem, situation, or person. "deal on" and "deal by" are not standard phrasal verbs with "deal."

Thus, the correct sentence is: "My uncle is a famous businessman who deals in antique home furniture."

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. He prefers drinking coffee / than tea in the morning / before he leaves / for his office.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

He prefers drinking coffee / than tea in the morning / before he leaves / for his office.
questions.solution:
The error lies in the use of the conjunction "than" after the verb "prefers." The verb "prefers" is followed by the preposition "to" when comparing two nouns or activities (gerunds). The construction is "prefers [something] to [something else]."

Correct sentence: He prefers drinking coffee to tea in the morning before he leaves for his office.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option b).

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

Note: Gerund: Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. A gerund can be either the subject or object of a sentence in English. Example: "Everybody enjoyed her dancing and singing at the party." The words 'dancing' and 'singing' are gerunds.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. He insisted on to go to the concert even though his parents had strictly forbidden him from doing so .
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

He insisted on to go to the concert even though his parents had strictly forbidden him from doing so.
questions.solution:
The error is in the structure following the preposition "on". A preposition is always followed by a noun or a noun form. The verb "go" after "on" should be in its gerund form ("going") to function as a noun. The use of an infinitive ("to go") after a preposition is incorrect in this context.

Correct sentence: He insisted on going to the concert even though his parents had strictly forbidden him from doing so.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Note:

Gerund: Gerund is a verb form that functions as a noun, ending in -ing. A gerund can be either the subject or object of a sentence in English. Example: "Everybody enjoyed her dancing and singing at the party." The words 'dancing' and 'singing' are gerunds.

Infinitive: The infinitive is the base form of a verb, often preceded by to.

Consider the sentences given below:

· To err is human. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to err' is the subject of the verb 'is']

· My father likes to cook. [like a noun, the infinitive 'to cook' is the object of the verb 'likes']

· To vote in elections is our right. [the infinitive 'to vote', like a noun, is the subject of the verb 'is', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (elections)]

· Radha went to the lake to fetch water. [the infinitive 'to fetch', like a noun, is the object of the verb 'went', but, like a verb, it also takes an object (water)]

· The above sentences illustrate various ways in which infinitives are used. It can both act as a noun and a verb.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Our new school building comprises of fifty classrooms, a large library, and two state-of-the-art computer labs .
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Our new school building comprises of fifty classrooms, a large library, and two state-of-the-art computer labs.
questions.solution:
The error is in the use of the preposition "of" after the verb "comprises". In the active voice, the verb "comprise" means 'to consist of' or 'to be made up of' and is not followed by a preposition. The singular subject 'building' agrees with the singular verb 'comprises'. The preposition "of" is used when "comprise" is used in the passive voice (e.g., "is comprised of").

Correct sentence: Our new school building comprises fifty classrooms, a large library, and two state-of-the-art computer labs.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My younger brother is surprisingly good _________ solving complex mathematical problems.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My younger brother is surprisingly good _________ solving complex mathematical problems.
questions.solution:
The context of the sentence is about having a skill or ability in a particular activity ("solving problems"). The blank requires a preposition that correctly follows the adjective "good" to denote skill.

The correct option is "at." The phrase "good at something" is the standard English phrase used to express that someone has a talent or skill in a particular area.

The other options are incorrect: "good in" is sometimes used, but "good at" is more precise for skills and activities. "good on" and "good with" (which is used for handling people or tools) are not used in this context.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "My younger brother is surprisingly good at solving complex mathematical problems."

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Our new office is situated / conveniently at the third floor / of the modern skyscraper / in the city centre.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

Our new office is situated / conveniently at the third floor / of the modern skyscraper / in the city centre.
questions.solution:
The error is in the use of the preposition "at" to refer to a specific floor of a building. The correct preposition to use for floors is "on." We say something is "on the first floor," "on the second floor," etc.

Correct sentence: Our new office is situated conveniently on the third floor of the modern skyscraper in the city centre.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option c).

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My uncle has been practising law in the high court since fifteen years with great success and reputation .
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My uncle has been practising law in the high court since fifteen years with great success and reputation.
questions.solution:
The error is in the use of the preposition "since". "Since" is used to denote a specific point in time in the past (e.g., since 2008, since Monday). "For" is used to denote a period or duration of time (e.g., for two hours, for ten years). As "fifteen years" is a period of time, the correct preposition is "for".

Correct sentence: My uncle has been practising law in the high court for fifteen years with great success and reputation.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The CEO will preside on the annual general meeting of the company tomorrow.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The CEO will preside on the annual general meeting of the company tomorrow.
questions.solution:
The error in the underlined segment is the use of the preposition "on" with the verb "preside." The correct preposition to follow "preside" is "over." The phrasal verb "preside over" means to be in charge of a formal meeting or ceremony.

Option a) over the annual general meeting is correct as it uses the correct preposition "over" to form the phrasal verb.

Option b) at the annual general meeting is incorrect. While "at" can be used for location, it does not form the correct phrasal verb with "preside."

Option c) in the annual general meeting is incorrect because of incorrect preposition again.

Option d) upon the annual general meeting is incorrect because of incorrect preposition again.

Correct Sentence: The CEO will preside over the annual general meeting of the company tomorrow.

Hence, the most appropriate choice is a) over the annual general meeting.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The new policy is not applicable for everyone in the organisation yet.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The new policy is not applicable for everyone in the organisation yet.
questions.solution:
The error in the underlined segment is the use of the preposition "for" after the adjective "applicable." The correct preposition to use is "to." The phrase "applicable to" someone or something is a fixed expression meaning that a rule or law affects them.

Option c) to everyone in the organisation is correct as it uses the correct preposition "to" with "applicable."

All other options are incorrect because of incorrect preposition usage.

Correct Sentence: The new policy is not applicable to everyone in the organisation yet.

Hence, the most appropriate choice is c) to everyone in the organisation.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The naughty child jumped _________ the river to retrieve his floating ball.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The naughty child jumped _________ the river to retrieve his floating ball.
questions.solution:
The sentence describes an action involving movement from one place (outside the river) to another (inside the river). The blank requires a preposition that correctly conveys this motion from outside to inside.

The correct option is "into." The preposition "into" is used to show movement towards the inside of a place.

The other options are incorrect: "in" is used to indicate a position or state of being already inside something (e.g., he was swimming in the river). "on" indicates a position on a surface. "at" indicates a specific point or location.

Thus, the correct sentence is: "The naughty child jumped into the river to retrieve his floating ball."

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. My father was very angry / on me for breaking / his favourite expensive vase / while playing cricket inside.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

My father was very angry / on me for breaking / his favourite expensive vase / while playing cricket inside.
questions.solution:
The error is in the use of the preposition "on" after "angry." When one is angry with a person, the correct preposition to use is "with." The preposition "at" is used when one is angry about a thing or a situation. Since the father is angry with a person ("me"), "with" should be used.

Correct sentence: My father was very angry with me for breaking his favourite expensive vase while playing cricket inside.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option c).

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The inheritance was fairly distributed between the five siblings according to the last will of their father .
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The inheritance was fairly distributed between the five siblings according to the last will of their father.
questions.solution:
The error is in the usage of the preposition "between". "Between" is typically used when referring to two people or things. When referring to more than two people or things, the correct preposition is "among". Since the inheritance is being distributed among five siblings, "among" should be used.

Correct sentence: The inheritance was fairly distributed among the five siblings according to the last will of their father.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The little girl was afraid from the big, barking dog in the neighbour's yard.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The little girl was afraid from the big, barking dog in the neighbour's yard.
questions.solution:
The error in the underlined segment is the use of the preposition "from" after the adjective "afraid." The correct preposition to follow "afraid" is "of." The phrase "afraid of" is a fixed expression used to indicate fear of someone or something.

Option a) of the big, barking dog is correct as it uses the correct preposition "of" with "afraid."

Option b) with the big, barking dog is incorrect. "Afraid with" is not a standard phrase.

Option c) by the big, barking dog is incorrect. "By" would be used in a passive voice construction like "She was frightened by the dog."

Option d) at the big, barking dog is incorrect. "Afraid at" is not a standard phrase.

Correct Sentence: The little girl was afraid of the big, barking dog in the neighbour's yard.

Hence, the most appropriate choice is a) of the big, barking dog.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The patient needs to be taken care of by a professional nurse at home.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The patient needs to be taken care of by a professional nurse at home.
questions.solution:
The underlined segment is grammatically correct. The phrasal verb "take care of" means to look after someone or something. In this passive voice construction ("needs to be taken care of"), the preposition "of" is a fixed part of the phrasal verb and must be retained. The agent is correctly introduced by the preposition "by."

Option d) No substitution required is the correct choice because the original phrase is grammatically and idiomatically correct.

Option a) after by a professional nurse is incorrect. The phrasal verb "look after" has a similar meaning, but "take care after" is not a standard phrase.

Option b) for by a professional nurse is incorrect. "Care for" means to like or love someone, or to look after them, but "take care for" is not the correct phrase here.

Option c) with by a professional nurse is incorrect because of inappropriate preposition again.

Hence, the most appropriate choice is d) No substitution required.
